key_insight: Mask-based benchmarks misrepresent image edits: many pixels inside object masks are unedited while meaningful, subtle changes outside masks are ignored. Reformulating tampering evaluation to pixel-level, meaning- and language-aware signals yields more accurate detection and evaluation for VLMs.
problem_solved: Fixes the misalignment between coarse object-mask labels and the true edit signal by moving tampering evaluation from region masks to pixel-grounded, semantics-aware labels and metrics.
method: Define a taxonomy of edit primitives (replace, remove, splice, inpaint, attribute change, colorization, etc.) and link each primitive to semantic intent and language descriptions.
Build a pixel-grounded benchmark that annotates edits at pixel resolution and pairs them with natural-language edit descriptions for VLM evaluation.
Design meaning-aware metrics and evaluation protocols that score alignment between predicted edits, pixel-level changes, and language descriptions (versus conventional mask IoU-based metrics).
impact: Enables more faithful, interpretable evaluation of VLMs on image tampering, improving model development for multimedia forensics, content authenticity, and downstream safety/robustness tasks.
visual_elements: Before/after image triplet with pixel-difference heatmap highlighting subtle edits missed by masks
Taxonomy diagram listing edit primitives with example icons and short language prompts
Bar/line chart comparing conventional mask-IoU metrics vs. new pixel-meaning metrics across methods
Worked example: image, natural-language edit description, ground-truth pixel map, and VLM prediction with metric scores
paper_title: From Masks to Pixels and Meaning: A New Taxonomy, Benchmark, and Metrics for VLM Image Tampering
paper_authors: Xinyi Shang, Yi Tang, Jiacheng Cui, Ahmed Elhagry, Salwa K. Al Khatib
